verdict.rationale: Smithery's docs describe a real publishing flow. You can publish a deployed server via its public HTTPS URL, local stdio servers are distributed as MCPB bundles, and each server gets a dedicated page where users discover and install it, with a manual server-card fallback when scanning fails. However, Smithery's own shutdown notice says accounts, API keys, the CLI/SDKs and the docs tree stopped working on 2026-10-31, leaving only a public non-proxied registry. Whether developers can still publish is therefore unclear. Missing for 10: evidence that publishing still works after the shutdown (accounts are gone), a documented current publishing path for the remaining public registry, and independent hands-on corroboration of the publish-to-install flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can publish my own MCP server on the platform for distribution, discovery, and installation by others

citations.quote: If you’ve already deployed an MCP server elsewhere, you can publish it directly on Smithery via the URL method.
Distribution — Get a dedicated server page where users can discover, try, and install your MCP from any client
For local stdio servers — Smithery distributes a pre-built MCPB bundle that clients download and run locally.
Smithery will remain as a public (non-proxied) MCP registry.
